items.note: Literally "good day"; the standard polite greeting during the day.
Casual. Also "Sveikas!" to a man, "Sveika!" to a woman.
A greeting when you arrive, not a goodbye.
Also "Labos nakties."
Neutral; works with anyone. Casual: "Iki!"
Spoken short form of "pasimatysime".
Literally "How is it going?"; fine with both tu and Jūs.
The reply to "Kaip sekasi?". Polite: "O Jums?"
Polite: "Koks Jūsų vardas?"
Ona is a common Lithuanian woman's name.
To a group or politely. To one man: "Sveikas atvykęs!", to one woman: "Sveika atvykusi!"
Also means "Here you are" and "You're welcome".
Literally "There's nothing to thank for". "Prašom" is also common.
To get attention or pass by; also a general "I'm sorry".
Literally "forgive me", to a friend. Polite: "Atleiskite."

items.note: Polite (Jūs). To a friend: "Gal gali man padėti?"

translations.vi: Bạn có thể nhắc lại được không?

items.note: "Gal" (maybe) makes the request softer. To a friend: "Gal gali pakartoti?"
"Ne" is written together with the verb.

translations.vi: Tôi nói được một chút tiếng Litva.

translations.fa: این را به لیتوانیایی چطور می‌گویند؟
translations.vi: Cái đó nói bằng tiếng Litva thế nào?
translations.en: How do you say that in Lithuanian?

items.note: Polite: "Iš kur Jūs esate?"
Polite: "Kur Jūs gyvenate?"
Literally "How many years to you?". Polite: "Kiek Jums metų?"
To a woman: "Ar tu tikra?"
For a feminine noun: "Kuri?"
Asked with concern. Polite: "Kas Jums yra?"
Literally "I want to eat". Also "Aš alkanas" (a woman: "Aš alkana").
Literally "I want to drink". Also "Ištroškau."
Polite: "Palaukite minutėlę."
Literally "It is cold to me"; the same for men and women.
"Namo" means "(to) home"; no verb of motion is needed.

translations.vi: Tôi đang tìm điện thoại của mình.

items.note: Literally "How many hours?"
Hours are said with ordinal numbers: "the third hour".
Days of the week are not capitalised.
Also "Kasdien."
Literally "yesterday evening"; "vakar naktį" is late at night.
Also "Kur yra tualetas?"; signs often say WC.
Direction "to the left" is "Į kairę."
Direction "to the right" is "Į dešinę."
Polite (Jūs). To a friend: "Eik tiesiai."
Spoken short form of "Einame!". By car or bus: "Važiuojam!"
The everyday word for a supermarket or grocery shop.

translations.en: Is there a pharmacy near here?

translations.vi: Cho tôi một ly cà phê.

items.note: "Vandens" means "some water".

translations.vi: Cho tôi xem thực đơn được không?

items.note: "Meniu" never changes its ending.
Said while pointing.
Literally "to health"; also said after someone sneezes.
A woman says: "Aš vegetarė."

translations.fa: یک میز برای دو نفر، لطفاً.
translations.es: Una mesa para dos, por favor.

A woman says: "Aš jau soti." Also "Prisivalgiau."
Literally "railway station"; people also just say "stotis".

translations.vi: Làm sao để đến sân bay?
translations.en: How do I get to the airport?

translations.vi: Chỗ này có ai ngồi chưa?

items.note: Literally "Is it free here?"
"Stotelė" is a stop; "stotis" is a station.

translations.vi: Đây là hộ chiếu của tôi.

A woman says: "Aš laiminga."
